sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Falls Township, PA?
sections.html:
Yes. A Falls Township owner can list the house, sell it privately, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases it in its present condition. The township does not require a home inspection, but a few resale steps still have to be finished before closing.

Falls is a suburban Philadelphia township on the Delaware River in Bucks County. Parts of Fairless Hills and Levittown lie inside it, and some addresses use Morrisville or Yardley as the mailing name even though they sit in Falls. The 2020 Census counted 34,716 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 34,282, a 1.3% dip from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: What shaped Falls Township, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The township's history explains its housing. It was chartered in 1692, and Morrisville left it to become a borough in 1804 and Tullytown in 1891. Fallsington, the crossroads village, has been in continuous use since the colonial period. William Penn began his Pennsbury Manor residence here in 1682, and the reconstructed site is open to the public.

Population stood at 3,540 in 1950 and 29,082 in 1960 as Fairless Hills and Levittown were built. Details a buyer will check:

  • Size and water: 26.6 square miles in all, of which 22.3 are land and 4.3 (16.11%) are water, with Biles Island, Martins Creek and Queen Anne Creek among its features.
  • Highways: US 1 crosses the north as a freeway, US 13 (the old King's Highway) runs north and south, and PA 32 starts at US 1 in the northeast.
  • Rail and bus: Amtrak's Northeast Corridor and SEPTA's Trenton Line pass through but stop nowhere inside the township. The nearest SEPTA Regional Rail station is Levittown, and SEPTA bus routes 127 and 128 serve Falls.
  • Road upkeep: of 131.48 public road miles, the township maintains 85.88.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Falls Township housing?
sections.html:
Falls Township's median owner-occupied home was valued at $361,900 for 2020 to 2024, and 72.9% of homes are owner-occupied. Median household income was $93,223 and median gross rent $1,465.

sections.h2: What does Falls Township require when a house is resold?
sections.html:
Falls requires certification of four major components before it issues a certificate of occupancy for a resale, and it does not require a township home inspection. A 2021 ordinance replaced the older resale inspection with certification of the heating system, chimney, sewer system and electrical panel. When the ordinance passed in January 2021, the township manager said a buyer's private inspection goes "far greater" than the township's, and that buyers are told of open violations or outstanding permit violations before they buy.

  • Who handles it: the Code Enforcement Department, which also processes building, electrical, plumbing and zoning permits.
  • Rentals: the same ordinance set up a rental inspection program, with yearly inspection of common areas at apartment complexes and an interior inspection of any unit occupied three years or longer.
  • Historic area: a Historic Architectural Review Board takes requests for review of plans, so ask whether your property falls under it.
  • Flood and fill rules: the township posts a flood hazard area permit application and a FEMA substantial improvement form, which matter for a house near the river or the creeks.

Ask the Code Enforcement Department which components your house must certify and whether any permit on the property was left open.

sections.h2: How does flood and storm risk affect a Falls Township sale?
sections.html:
With 16% of its area under water and a ground elevation near 13 feet at the Falls climate station, drainage and flood history are fair questions from buyers. Falls has a humid subtropical climate with about 47.78 inches of precipitation a year, and July is the wettest month. The wettest day since 1981 was August 27, 2011, with 6.49 inches. The highest temperature since 1981 was 103.4 degrees on June 7, 2010.

List what you know about basement water, sump pumps and past claims on the disclosure form. If your house has had repairs after storms, keep the permits and invoices for the buyer, and ask the township whether a flood hazard permit applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: How do Bucks County assessments, appeals and exclusions work for a Falls seller?
sections.html:
The Bucks County Board of Assessment Appeals sets values and hears appeals, from its office at 55 East Court Street in Doylestown. The deadline for 2026 annual appeals was August 3, 2026, with a non-refundable $75 fee per parcel, and any change takes effect for the 2027 tax year. The board meets at 10 a.m. on the first and third Tuesdays of each month.

Evidence of value can be an appraisal by a Pennsylvania certified appraiser or sales of similar nearby properties within the last 18 months. A buyer who closed within 18 months can attach the settlement sheet, though it cannot be the only evidence.

  • Homestead: the application for the tax year beginning July 1, 2027 is due March 1, 2027, and any new recorded deed requires a new application within 45 days.
  • Buyer's duty: under Act 29, a new owner must give the board contact information within 30 days of purchase.

Tell a buyer about the 45-day homestead rule, since a new deed resets the exclusion.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and state disclosure rules apply in Falls Township?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania imposes a 1% realty transfer tax that the county Recorder of Deeds collects along with any local tax. Exempt transfers include certain family transfers and property passing by testate or intestate succession, and 15% of collections go to the Keystone Recreation, Park and Conservation Fund. Ask the Recorder for the local rate on your price.

On the disclosure side, 68 Pa.C.S. section 7312 lets a seller amend a disclosure in writing before the agreement is signed, and section 7307 requires the seller to tell the buyer if facts change before final settlement. A "material defect" means a problem with a significant adverse effect on value or an unreasonable risk to people, and a system near the end of its useful life is not one by itself. A municipality cannot require extra disclosures beyond the statute, except under ordinances in place before the law took effect.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Falls Township?
sections.html: It fits when you want to avoid the certification steps, repair bids and a buyer's financing contingency. Typical Falls Township cases are an inherited house, a house with a failed heating or sewer system that blocks the resale certificate, a rental that would fail a township inspection, or a move on a fixed date. Compare the offer with a listing's net after repairs and transfer tax.

faqs.q: Does Falls Township require a home inspection to sell?
faqs.a: No. The township replaced its resale inspection with certification of the heating system, chimney, sewer system and electrical panel, and it left any private home inspection to the buyer and seller.

faqs.q: What happens if one of the four components fails?
faqs.a: The certificate of occupancy waits until the item is certified. Ask the Code Enforcement Department what repair or permit it needs, or sell as-is to a buyer who will complete it.

faqs.q: When was the Bucks County appeal deadline in 2026?
faqs.a: August 3, 2026, which has passed. Annual appeals are filed with the Board of Assessment Appeals, cost $75 per parcel and change the assessment for the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: Are Levittown and Fairless Hills part of Falls Township?
faqs.a: Parts of both are. Portions of Fairless Hills and Levittown lie inside the township, and the Morrisville and Yardley post office names also cover some Falls addresses.

faqs.q: How long does a fast sale take in Falls Township?
faqs.a: The closing date is set by the contract, and a cash buyer does not wait for a lender. Title work, any open permits and the resale certificate steps set the earliest date.
